newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 23 to 840 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 23 to 840 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 840 this week, down 23 from last week but 133 above the 707 a year ago, oilfield services company Baker Hughes Inc. said Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by 22 to 709, while rigs working offshore fell two to 104. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose one to 27.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Oklahoma, where the number of rigs fell 10, Louisiana, which was down four and Pennsylvania, which was down three.
A total of 357 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up three from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell 27 to 481, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects doubled to two.
There were 158 rigs drilling directionally, 69 drilling horizontally and 613 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was down eight at 404 versus 374 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, there were 168 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Feb. 28, unchanged from the period ending Feb. 21, Offshore Data Services said.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 184, was 91.3 percent.
